title: Machine and Orbit
premise: Odile Voss, a xenolinguist whose mind was permanently altered by contact with an alien signal seven years ago, has hidden among cargo haulers in contested orbits to escape the Consortium that wants her back. When the research ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew biologically reversed—aged backward into children carrying adult memories—Odile realizes the alien signal she decoded is a countdown, and the Halcyon's data holds the key to which half of humanity can be saved when it reaches zero. Torn between her loyalty to her crew and the truth that only she can read, Odile races the Consortium and the clock itself. In the end, she sacrifices her own place in cryosleep, translating the final message so that both halves of humanity wake—not saved, but changed—and she becomes the bridge between them.
about_author: Silas Almeida is a former radio astronomer who spent a decade listening to deep space before turning to fiction about what might listen back. He writes from a converted observatory on the Atlantic coast, where he claims the static still talks to him.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Odile Voss hauls contraband water ice through the Meridian Belt aboard the freighter Long Silence, hiding the fact that she no longer dreams in any human language. Her captain, Rhee, suspects she's more than she claims. The chapter establishes her isolation and the fragile loyalty of her found crew. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: The Halcyon docks at Ceres Station, its crew of forty reduced to children with adult eyes. Odile recognizes the signal patterns in their neural scans—the same ones haunting her dreams for seven years. POV shifts between Odile and Dr. Amara Chen, the Halcyon's de-aged xenobiologist. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: What the Consortium Wants
chapters.summary: Consortium agents board Ceres hunting 'the Voss anomaly.' Rhee covers for Odile but demands answers; she confesses she decoded an alien transmission years ago and has been running ever since. The agents take the Halcyon's data core. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust by necessity, and the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: Dreams in No Human Tongue
chapters.summary: In flashback-heavy chapters of memory, Odile reconstructs the original contact: a signal that rewrote her language centers, leaving her fluent in something no one else can hear. She realizes the signal is a countdown tied to the Halcyon's trajectory. POV: Odile alone. Emotional beat: grief for the self she lost to understanding.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Stars
chapters.summary: Odile smuggles herself aboard the quarantined Halcyon and meets the child-crew. Young Amara Chen, eight years old with thirty years of memories, reveals the ship found something at the signal's source—a structure, and a choice encoded inside it. Emotional beat: tenderness toward broken people, and the horror of stolen time.

chapters.title: Two Arcologies, One Door
chapters.summary: The countdown's meaning emerges: Earth's orbital habitats can shield only half the population from the coming solar event the aliens engineered—or offer passage through the structure instead. The Consortium plans to decide who lives by wealth and rank. Odile holds the translation they need. Emotional beat: rage at power deciding whose breath counts.

chapters.title: The Price of Loyalty
chapters.summary: Rhee sells Odile's location to the Consortium to save his crew from reprisal—but then turns his guns on the agents instead, choosing her over safety. The Long Silence barely escapes Ceres burning behind them. A crew member dies holding the airlock. Emotional beat: loyalty proven costly, love declared in gunfire.

chapters.title: The Structure Speaks
chapters.summary: Following the Halcyon's original trajectory, Odile reaches the alien structure and discovers the 'choice' was never a selection—it was an invitation to merge human consciousness with the signal itself, becoming translators who could carry all of humanity through. It requires one mind already fluent. Hers. Emotional beat: terror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: The Consortium fleet arrives to seize the structure; the solar event begins early. Odile enters the interface as Rhee and young Amara hold the docking ring against boarding parties. Inside, she bargains with the signal's intelligence—not surrendering, but negotiating, linguist to architect. Climax: she rewrites the terms mid-translation. Emotional beat: defiance as devotion.

chapters.title: A Language We Wake Into
chapters.summary: Both arcologies survive, transformed—humanity wakes changed, able to perceive the signal directly, neither saved nor conquered but partnered. Odile's body remains in the structure, yet her voice now speaks through every dream. Rhee and Amara carry her story home. Final beat: love against duty resolved—she chose everyone, and everyone remembers her name.
